builds.name: Reference: Ranked mid core
builds.goal: Reference for Sylas: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ mid players use most (8,406 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 50.2% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A spell-and-attack melee skirmisher who cycles empowered attacks and healing, adapting his ultimate options to enemy champions. The current mid provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Hextech Rocketbelt → Riftmaker → Zhonya's Hourglass. Conqueror keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Sorcerer's Shoes, Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff.
builds.summary: The proven mid baseline: Hextech Rocketbelt → Riftmaker → Zhonya's Hourglass, with Conqueror.
testPlan: Play it in mid as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Hextech Rocketbelt → Riftmaker → Zhonya's Hourglass) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 50.2% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Hextech Rocketbelt → Riftmaker → Zhonya's Hourglass.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula:
After using an Ability, Sylas gains a charge (max [rankTable[2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3]] charges). Sylas' Attacks expend a charge to whirl his chains, dealing [(1.3) × AD + (0.3) × AP] magic damage to the main target and [(0.4) × AD + (0.2) × AP] magic damage to other surrounding enemies.

While he has at least one charge, Sylas gains [125]% Attack Speed.

Sylas lunges at an enemy with magical force dealing [75 / 110 / 145 / 180 / 215 + (0.6) × AP] magic damage. Against champions, Sylas restores between [20 / 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 + (0.3) × AP + (0.05) × Stat(12)[statFormula=2]] and [(20 / 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 + (0.3) × AP + (0.05) × Stat(12)[statFormula=2]) × (2)] Health based on his missing Health (max healing at or below [40]% Health).

Sylas hijacks an enemy champion, allowing him to cast a copy of their ultimate Ability, based on his Ultimate level and using his stats.

Hijacking an enemy places a Cooldown on them for [(runtimeCooldownMultiplier) × (200)]% (modified by Sylas' Ability Haste) of the enemy's ultimate's Cooldown, with a minimum of [40] seconds, during which time Sylas cannot hijack them again.

Sylas lashes his chains out, dealing [40 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 120 + (0.4) × AP] magic damage and Slowing by [0.15 / 0.2 / 0.25 / 0.3 / 0.35] for [1.5] seconds. The place where the chains intersect explodes, dealing a further [60 / 115 / 170 / 225 / 280 + (0.8) × AP] magic damage.

Sylas quickly dashes, and prepares a Recast for 3.5 seconds.

Recast: Sylas throws his chains, pulling himself to the first enemy hit, dealing [80 / 130 / 180 / 230 / 280 + (0.8) × AP] magic damage, and Knocking Up for [0.5] seconds.

builds.name: Health Kingslayer return
builds.summary: Use bonus health to support a second low-health W rather than a single burst.
builds.goal: Use bonus health to support a second low-health W rather than a single burst.
builds.hypothesis: W healing includes AP and a bonus-health Stat term, doubling toward low health. Riftmaker turns bonus health into AP and Visage increases received healing; Cosmic helps stay close and Dusk rewards attacks between casts. E access and charge attacks are still necessary to maintain contact.
testPlan: Required state: W targets a champion, current health recorded and enough time for a second W.
Measure W heal at above and below 40% health with matched bonus health, then record second-cast access.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Grievous Wounds or burst before the second cast defeats the sustain budget.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Kingslayer's champion heal does not apply identically against minions.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Riftmaker, Spirit Visage, Cosmic Drive, Dusk and Dawn, Rabadon's Deathcap, Mercury's Treads. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Survive the engage
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Sylas: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A spell-and-attack melee skirmisher who cycles empowered attacks and healing, adapting his ultimate options to enemy champions. Measure empowered passive attacks and W healing with a specified stolen R. Do not average every enemy ultimate into one guaranteed burst/utility result. A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
builds.summary: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
testPlan: Kit question for Sylas: Measure empowered passive attacks and W healing with a specified stolen R. Do not average every enemy ultimate into one guaranteed burst/utility result.

Start with the early core (Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Sylas lashes his chains out, intersecting at his targeted location dealing damage to and slowing enemies. 

After a delay, magical energy explodes from the intersection point dealing damage. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.
The route fails Sylas's stated kit question: Measure empowered passive attacks and W healing with a specified stolen R. Do not average every enemy ultimate into one guaranteed burst/utility result.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.
Full cost 16,000 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Banshee's Veil, Rylai's Crystal Scepter, Void Staff are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Petricite AD ratio
builds.summary: Test AD on the passive's main-target magic attack conversion.
builds.goal: Test AD on the passive's main-target magic attack conversion.
builds.hypothesis: Petricite Burst converts a main-target attack using 1.3 AD and 0.3 AP, while charged state gives 125% attack speed. Trinity, Titanic and Bloodmail test a health/AD attack budget; Abyssal supports nearby passive magic damage while Titanic supplies separate physical packets. Hijacked R selection remains opponent dependent.
testPlan: Required state: Cast then spend passive charges instead of overflowing the charge cap, with finite bonus health.
Separate main-target passive magic damage, splash and item physical damage after one cast at matched total AD.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Losing AP weakens W/Q/E and converted magic attacks gain nothing from armor penetration.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Passive's magic conversion does not prove it carries every ordinary attack or crit rule.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.

Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
